title: Democrat Scott Colom Wins Mississippi Senate Race, AP Calls
dek: Democrat Scott Colom has won Mississippi’s U.S. Senate race over Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, the AP called Wednesday, making him the state’s first Black senator since Reconstruction.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Old Mississippi State Capitol building in Jackson, Mississippi

keyPoints: The Associated Press called the Mississippi Senate race for Democrat Scott Colom on Wednesday, Nov. 11, after counties updated results and provisional ballots were processed.
Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, 67, called Colom late Wednesday afternoon to concede.
Colom, a 43-year-old local prosecutor, will be Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction, AP reported.
AP wrote that the last time Mississippi chose a new Democratic senator was 1947, when the winner was a staunch segregationist.
body:
Democrat Scott Colom has won Mississippi's U.S. Senate race, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith, the [Associated Press reported](https://apnews.com/article/race-call-colom-wins-mississippi-u-s-senate-1787bf4967fd46cfbed2fe4d777a5781). The AP called the race Wednesday, Nov. 11, after more than a week of counting outstanding absentee ballots, [NPR reported](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/11/g-s1-151688/mississippi-senate-race-scott-colom).

## Why the call came when it did

The AP declared Colom the winner after several counties reported updated results, including provisional ballots, the wire service said in a separate [explainer](https://apnews.com/article/mississippi-senate-colom-hydesmith-midterm-7f098b8834f598c923ba73572ea2223f). [Mississippi Today reported](https://mississippitoday.org/2026/11/11/why-ap-called-mississippi-senate-race-scott-colom/) that the call came just before 5 p.m. CT, after officials in Jackson County updated their count with an additional 2,173 votes.

## Concession

Hyde-Smith, 67, called Colom late Wednesday afternoon to concede and later released a concession statement. "While this is not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said, according to AP. She also wished Colom well as he "takes on the tremendous responsibility of representing our great state."

## A historic first

Colom, a 43-year-old local prosecutor, will be Mississippi's first Black senator since the post-Civil War Reconstruction era, AP reported. The AP also wrote that the last time Mississippi chose a new Democratic senator was 1947, and that the winner was a staunch segregationist.

Mississippi has the largest share of Black residents of any U.S. state, AP noted, yet its politics have been controlled mostly by white conservatives for generations.

## Campaign context

AP reported that Colom capitalized on the state's large Black population, discontent with the economy and Hyde-Smith's missteps as she sought a second full term. AP described the result as adding to a midterm rebuke of President Donald Trump, whose party suffered defeats in several Republican-controlled states. The outcome will bolster some Democrats' argument that their future runs through the American South, AP wrote.

Speaking to a crowd of hundreds at Tougaloo College in Jackson, Colom said, "I had the courage to believe in Mississippi." During the campaign, he said he could represent all of Mississippi, and he repeated that pledge after the call. "My commitment to you, each and every one of you, is that first I'm going to treat your children like I want my children to be treated," he said, AP reported.
